newsitem.title: BRAZIL: One fifth of Rio residents can't name president-poll.
newsitem.headline: One fifth of Rio residents can't name president-poll.

text.p: One fifth of the voting age population in greater Rio de Janeiro can not name Fernando Henrique Cardoso as the president of Brazil, according to a poll published on Sunday.

The survey, conducted by the Rio think tank Getulio Vargas Foundation, also found that 30 percent of the 1,578 people surveyed could not identify Rio state Gov Marcelo Alencar and 31.5 percent could not name the mayor of their municipality.

The survey, conducted between December 1995 and August 1996 but whose results were not released until Sunday, was published in the Rio de Janeiro daily newspaper Jornal do Brasil. It did not provide a margin of error.

Pollsters said they were somewhat baffled by the results, noting that 97 percent of the respondents had a television in their home and that many said they watched news programmes at least five times a week.
"It's as if people just tune out of the country's political problems, which they do not think is a subject that should interest them," Dulce Pandolfi, one of the pollsters, told Jornal do Brasil.
